aria: Animated recap of the Nuggets' 123 to 118 road win over the Grizzlies: Cameron Johnson's 3-pointer off a Nikola Jokić kickout with 1:01 left that made it 120 to 113, quarter-by-quarter scoring, Jamal Murray's 30 points with 17 in the fourth quarter, the top scorers, how the Nuggets won, and the next game at New Orleans.

notes: Box score from the Nuggets' 123–118 win over the Memphis Grizzlies at FedExForum on Nov 11, 2026, from the Covers.com box score, with game details from the Associated Press (via Denver7 and WRAL), the Denver Gazette, DenverSports.com, Denver Stiffs and Plain Text Sports (halftime). All 123 Denver points and all 118 Memphis points are accounted for in the box score, and the quarter scores add up to both totals (65–52 at the half, matching Plain Text Sports and the Denver Gazette). Denver's 18-point lead and Memphis never leading are from Covers and the AP. Assists (34–27), points in the paint (54–40), blocks (11–4), free throws (11–19) and bench points (22–44) are from the Covers box score; Denver's 6 turnovers and points off turnovers (15–2) are from the Denver Gazette. Records and ranks are from the site's standings after Wednesday's games: Denver 6–4 and tenth in the West, New Orleans 4–8.

Memphis won the third quarter 38–29 and got within one before Murray scored 17 in the fourth on 7-of-8 shooting (AP); it is his fifth 30-point game this season (Denver Gazette, DenverSports.com). Nine different Nuggets had a block (Denver Gazette; the box score agrees). Denver plays at New Orleans on Saturday at 7:00 PM ET (AP); it beat the Pelicans 141–135 on Oct 24 and 104–91 on Oct 28 (2026–27 Nuggets season page on Wikipedia; AP via WLOX).

The play of the game is an original illustration of Cameron Johnson's 3-pointer off a Nikola Jokić pass with 1:01 left, which made it 120–113 (AP; DenverSports.com calls it a Jokić kickout 3 with 1:01 left). Johnson's driving layup just before had made it 117–113 (Denver Stiffs). The recaps don't describe how he got the shot beyond the kickout, so it is drawn as the template's plain pull-up. A play-by-play could not be reached this morning, so the clock and score rest on those written accounts. The figures are stylized and not traced from footage, and the spacing is not to scale.

The music is an original beat made for this page. No existing recordings or melodies are used. This is an unofficial fan recap, not affiliated with the Denver Nuggets or the NBA, which is why it carries a plain basketball mark and the team's colors but not the team's logo.

The shooter in the play of the game is drawn to Johnson's listed 6-foot-8 and 210 pounds (RealGM), in Denver's road navy with No. 23. No measured wingspan has been reported, so his arms are drawn at his height. He has no approved look on file yet, so he is drawn as a team-colour silhouette in the kit. It is an original silhouette with a featureless face, not a portrait or a trace of footage.
